1. Recovery can move the project checkout 🐞 Bug ☼ Reliability
>
>Description >
> >
>is_stale_state_worktree identifies the project checkout through the process's current directory
>rather than the directory it is about to move. If ROOM_STATE_DIR names a detached project checkout
>and the command runs from elsewhere, ensure_worktree can rename that checkout and replace its path
>with a state worktree, disrupting linked builder worktrees.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[room.py[R641-642]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/pull/6/files#diff-36e706accba1fe5812fd1526e9931f792f8e314ada3f00e0e24e85cd44fb2433R641-R642) > >```diff >+ top = project_toplevel() >+ return not (top and os.path.realpath(top) == os.path.realpath(path)) >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The checkout comparison uses project_toplevel() for the current process, not the candidate path.
>The included scoped review documents a reproduction in which recovery moves the project checkout and
>breaks its builder worktree.
>
> > [room.py\[624-642\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/870f10beea0d145859842b5a254b52c98d2cfb39/room.py/#L624-L642) > [room.py\[671-695\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/870f10beea0d145859842b5a254b52c98d2cfb39/room.py/#L671-L695) > [reviews/cold/M2/scoped-1.md\[14-14\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/870f10beea0d145859842b5a254b52c98d2cfb39/reviews/cold/M2/scoped-1.md/#L14-L14) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >Stale-directory recovery can mistake the project checkout for a disposable state worktree when invoked outside that checkout. >## Fix Focus Areas >- room.py[624-660] >- room.py[671-695] >## Recommended Fix >Inspect the candidate directory's own Git metadata to distinguish the project's main checkout from a managed state worktree, regardless of the invoking directory. Refuse uncertain directories before renaming or resetting them. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

2. A damaged block restores an old lead 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>STATE_BLOCK can treat a later fence as the missing closing fence, and read_block accepts the
>first parseable matching block even if it is a quoted copy below the real one. After an outside edit
>damages either fence, an old lease copied into mission notes can become authoritative without a
>warning, allowing a superseded lead to post, close the room, or reuse a counter.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[room.py[R553-554]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/pull/6/files#diff-36e706accba1fe5812fd1526e9931f792f8e314ada3f00e0e24e85cd44fb2433R553-R554) > >```diff >+STATE_BLOCK = re.compile(r"^```agent-room-state[ \t]*\n(.*?)^```[ \t]*$", re.M | re.S) >+BROKEN_BLOCK = re.compile(r"^```[ \t]*agent-room-state\b[^\n]*\n.*?^```[ \t]*$\n?", re.M | re.S) # a damaged fence >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The regular expression may span to a later fence, and the parser accepts a matching block wherever
>it finds one. The included scoped review reproduces both damaged-fence cases and shows a superseded
>lead gaining the lease.
>
> > [room.py\[553-555\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/870f10beea0d145859842b5a254b52c98d2cfb39/room.py/#L553-L555) > [room.py\[841-850\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/870f10beea0d145859842b5a254b52c98d2cfb39/room.py/#L841-L850) > [reviews/cold/M2/scoped-3.md\[11-12\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/870f10beea0d145859842b5a254b52c98d2cfb39/reviews/cold/M2/scoped-3.md/#L11-L12) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >Malformed fences or a quoted second block can make the current state appear to grant the lease to a superseded lead. >## Fix Focus Areas >- room.py[553-554] >- room.py[839-850] >- room.py[941-965] >## Recommended Fix >Require one canonical machine block in the expected position, with a correctly closed fence and only valid body lines. Reject ambiguous or damaged tips so lease reads fall back to the last valid commit; refuse duplicate blocks on commit. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

3. Block repair erases mission records 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>BROKEN_BLOCK can span from a damaged opening fence to a later fence in the mission notes, and
>with_block replaces that entire span with a restored block. If an outside edit also removes the
>block's closing fence, the next state write can delete intervening mission tables, tasks, and parked
>questions from the pushed file.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[room.py[R882-884]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/pull/6/files#diff-36e706accba1fe5812fd1526e9931f792f8e314ada3f00e0e24e85cd44fb2433R882-R884) > >```diff >+ m = BROKEN_BLOCK.search(text) >+ if m: >+ return text[:m.start()] + block + text[m.end():] >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The replacement uses the entire BROKEN_BLOCK match as its deletion range. The scoped review
>records a repair that removed the mission table and task records after both fences were damaged.
>
> > [room.py\[553-554\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/870f10beea0d145859842b5a254b52c98d2cfb39/room.py/#L553-L554) > [room.py\[873-888\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/870f10beea0d145859842b5a254b52c98d2cfb39/room.py/#L873-L888) > [reviews/cold/M2/scoped-3.md\[13-13\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/870f10beea0d145859842b5a254b52c98d2cfb39/reviews/cold/M2/scoped-3.md/#L13-L13) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >Repairing a block with damaged fences can consume and delete mission records below it. >## Fix Focus Areas >- room.py[553-554] >- room.py[873-888] >## Recommended Fix >Do not replace text through an inferred later closing fence when the original boundary is uncertain. Prepend a valid canonical block and retire the damaged fence while preserving all existing prose. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

4. One lead can hide messages from another 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>unseen now distinguishes leads by session, but cursor_file still stores one cursor per room and
>role. When two lead sessions share a machine, the first lead's read advances the second lead's
>cursor past architect messages that the second has not seen.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[room.py[319]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/pull/6/files#diff-36e706accba1fe5812fd1526e9931f792f8e314ada3f00e0e24e85cd44fb2433R319-R319) > >```diff >+ others = [m for m in fresh if not is_own(m, role, sid)] >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The cursor filename omits session, while the changed filtering treats another session of the same
>role as a message recipient and saves the cursor beyond all fresh comments.
>
> > [room.py\[266-283\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/870f10beea0d145859842b5a254b52c98d2cfb39/room.py/#L266-L283) > [room.py\[302-325\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/870f10beea0d145859842b5a254b52c98d2cfb39/room.py/#L302-L325) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >Two sessions of the same role share a cursor even though messages are now hidden per session. >## Fix Focus Areas >- room.py[266-288] >- room.py[302-326] >## Recommended Fix >Key read and wait cursors by room, role, and validated session ID. Update cursor moves and reads consistently, with a deliberate migration path for existing role-only cursors. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

5. Weakened tests evade the merge hold 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>The M3 gate specification says a merge-hold bullet containing deleted matches only deleted paths,
>while the default playbook puts deleted and weakened tests in that same bullet. An edit to an
>existing test therefore matches the test globs but does not trigger the sensitive-path hold required
>by the governing design.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[docs/design/m3-reviews-gate.md[109]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/pull/6/files#diff-1d80bc747f61196b20f463418d4f5a8ed63e17504c309ba79834aa3278ce332fR109-R109) > >```diff >+6. **Sensitive paths:** the changed paths (`git diff --name-status origin/main...HEAD`) against the globs of the "## Merge-hold list" section of `PLAYBOOK.md` on the state branch. The template has one bullet per area, ``-
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The new specification excludes non-deletions for the template's combined test bullet, whereas v1
>includes weakened tests among sensitive changes and requires matching paths to fail the gate.
>
> > [docs/design/m3-reviews-gate.md\[108-109\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/870f10beea0d145859842b5a254b52c98d2cfb39/docs/design/m3-reviews-gate.md/#L108-L109) > [templates/playbook/PLAYBOOK.md\[23-31\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/870f10beea0d145859842b5a254b52c98d2cfb39/templates/playbook/PLAYBOOK.md/#L23-L31) > [docs/design/v1.md\[215-229\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/870f10beea0d145859842b5a254b52c98d2cfb39/docs/design/v1.md/#L215-L229) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >The deleted-only rule exempts modified tests from the default sensitive-path hold, including modifications that weaken them. >## Fix Focus Areas >- docs/design/m3-reviews-gate.md[108-109] >- templates/playbook/PLAYBOOK.md[27-31] >## Recommended Fix >Specify a conservative hold for modified tests unless a reliable weakened-test determination is available. Keep the template labels and gate matching rules aligned with that behavior. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

6. Recovery strands unpushed state commits 🐞 Bug ☼ Reliability
>
>Description >
> >
>ensure_worktree moves a stale linked state worktree aside without checking whether it contains
>local changes or unpushed commits. When it prunes and recreates the worktree at the original path,
>the moved copy's Git administrative link can point at the replacement, leaving its earlier commit
>without a normal ref or reflog.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[room.py[679]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/pull/6/files#diff-36e706accba1fe5812fd1526e9931f792f8e314ada3f00e0e24e85cd44fb2433R679-R679) > >```diff >+ move_aside(path, f"is stale (no history of the recreated {STATE_BRANCH})") >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The stale path is moved without a pending-work check, then the linked worktree is pruned and
>recreated. The scoped review records the resulting loss of the old commit's refs and reflog.
>
> > [room.py\[663-695\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/870f10beea0d145859842b5a254b52c98d2cfb39/room.py/#L663-L695) > [reviews/cold/M2/scoped-1.md\[13-13\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/870f10beea0d145859842b5a254b52c98d2cfb39/reviews/cold/M2/scoped-1.md/#L13-L13) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >Rebuilding a stale linked worktree can strand commits and obscure local changes that were never pushed. >## Fix Focus Areas >- room.py[663-695] >- room.py[705-728] >## Recommended Fix >Detect and clearly report pending changes before recovery. Preserve the stale worktree's HEAD under a durable ref or standalone repository, and do not reuse its Git administrative entry until its local history is recoverable. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

7. A lead inside stale state cannot recover 🐞 Bug ☼ Reliability
>
>Description >
> >
>ensure_worktree rebuilds a stale state directory while Git commands and checkout discovery still
>depend on the invoking directory. When a lead runs a state command from inside a state worktree
>whose branch was recreated, clone-mode recovery can refuse it and linked-worktree recovery can fail
>partway through after moving it.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[room.py[679]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/pull/6/files#diff-36e706accba1fe5812fd1526e9931f792f8e314ada3f00e0e24e85cd44fb2433R679-R679) > >```diff >+ move_aside(path, f"is stale (no history of the recreated {STATE_BRANCH})") >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>Checkout discovery and candidate recognition depend on cwd while recovery renames the candidate. The
>scoped review provides both clone-mode and linked-worktree reproductions from inside that directory.
>
> > [room.py\[624-642\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/870f10beea0d145859842b5a254b52c98d2cfb39/room.py/#L624-L642) > [room.py\[671-698\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/870f10beea0d145859842b5a254b52c98d2cfb39/room.py/#L671-L698) > [reviews/cold/M2/scoped-1.md\[15-15\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/870f10beea0d145859842b5a254b52c98d2cfb39/reviews/cold/M2/scoped-1.md/#L15-L15) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >The stale-worktree rebuild path does not work when the process is running inside the directory being replaced. >## Fix Focus Areas >- room.py[624-642] >- room.py[671-698] >## Recommended Fix >Resolve and retain a valid project repository or remote before moving the stale directory. Run recovery Git operations from that stable location, and recognize the candidate state directory independently of the invoking cwd. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

8. Preflight can report no admin bypass when it couldn't read the ruleset 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>cmd_preflight stores {} for a failed or non-dict ruleset-detail response without recording that
>the ruleset could not be inspected. When branch rules identify that ruleset, the bypass check finds
>no actors in the empty dictionary and can print ✓ admin bypass: none instead of an unknown
>warning, because its existing error path covers only protection and branch-rules requests.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[room.py[R1240-1243]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/pull/6/files#diff-36e706accba1fe5812fd1526e9931f792f8e314ada3f00e0e24e85cd44fb2433R1240-R1243) > >```diff >+ rid = rule.get("ruleset_id") >+ if rid is not None and rid not in rulesets: >+ s, rs = gh_try(f"repos/{REPO}/rulesets/{rid}") >+ rulesets[rid] = rs if s == 200 and isinstance(rs, dict) else {} >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>Failures from the protection and branch-rules requests are recorded, but failures from individual
>ruleset-detail requests become empty dictionaries. The bypass section reads actors from those
>dictionaries, so when branch rules are present and no other request failed, it reaches `✓ admin
>bypass: none` despite not having read every ruleset's bypass list.
>
> > [room.py\[1238-1243\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/870f10beea0d145859842b5a254b52c98d2cfb39/room.py/#L1238-L1243) > [room.py\[1267-1284\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/870f10beea0d145859842b5a254b52c98d2cfb39/room.py/#L1267-L1284) > [room.py\[1224-1243\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/870f10beea0d145859842b5a254b52c98d2cfb39/room.py/#L1224-L1243) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >A failed or non-dict ruleset-detail response is treated as though the ruleset has no bypass actors, allowing preflight to report `admin bypass: none` without inspecting it. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- room.py[1238-1243] >- room.py[1267-1284] > >## Recommended Fix >Track referenced rulesets whose detail requests return a non-200 status or a non-dict response in an `unreadable` list, separately from successfully read rulesets. When that list is non-empty, make the bypass check print `! admin bypass: unknown for (report only)` instead of `✓ admin bypass: none`. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
[Dismiss ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/344ffc3b-f7a2-46c9-8cdf-8b7374d70556?action=dismiss&origin=git) | [View ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/344ffc3b-f7a2-46c9-8cdf-8b7374d70556)

9. Preflight --fix failure prints no reason 🐞 Bug ◔ Observability
>
>Description >
> >
>The --fix handler formats {e or 'the state branch moved; run it again'}, but an exception object
>is always truthy, so a bare StateMoved() (empty message) wins over the fallback. When the
>lead-files push loses a race during preflight --fix, the output reads `lead-owned files: --fix
>failed: ` with no explanation and no hint to retry.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[room.py[R1335-1336]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/pull/6/files#diff-36e706accba1fe5812fd1526e9931f792f8e314ada3f00e0e24e85cd44fb2433R1335-R1336) > >```diff >+ except (StateError, StateMoved) as e: >+ check("✗", f"lead-owned files: --fix failed: {e or 'the state branch moved; run it again'}") >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>commit_and_push raises StateMoved() with no message. add_missing reaches it through preflight,
>and the handler's e or ... never chooses the fallback string because exception objects are truthy.
>
> > [room.py\[766-768\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/870f10beea0d145859842b5a254b52c98d2cfb39/room.py/#L766-L768) > [room.py\[1331-1336\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/870f10beea0d145859842b5a254b52c98d2cfb39/room.py/#L1331-L1336) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >Preflight `--fix` prints an empty reason when `StateMoved` is raised, because `e or '...'` tests the exception object, which is always truthy. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- room.py[1335-1336] > >## Recommended Fix >Replace `{e or 'the state branch moved; run it again'}` with `{str(e) or 'the state branch moved; run it again'}`, or catch `StateMoved` in its own `except` branch with that message. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
[Dismiss ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/34971e39-52d9-4e93-967c-2d49f278cc08?action=dismiss&origin=git) | [View ↗](https://app.qodo.ai/findings/34971e39-52d9-4e93-967c-2d49f278cc08)
10. A failed git diff makes state commit report 'nothing to commit' 🐞 Bug ☼ Reliability
>
>Description >
> >
>commit_and_push runs git diff --cached --quiet with check=False and commits only when it
>returns exactly 1. Any other failure, such as exit 128 from a broken index, is treated as 'no staged
>changes'. With no unpushed commits, state commit then prints nothing to commit and exits 0,
>while the edits stay unpushed in the worktree.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[room.py[R750-753]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/pull/6/files#diff-36e706accba1fe5812fd1526e9931f792f8e314ada3f00e0e24e85cd44fb2433R750-R753) > >```diff >+ if git("diff", "--cached", "--quiet", cwd=path, check=False).returncode == 1: >+ git(*identity(path), "commit", "-q", "-m", msg, cwd=path) >+ if git_out("rev-list", "--count", f"{STATE_REF}..HEAD", cwd=path) == "0": >+ return False # no local commits; the remote may be ahead, which is not ours to push >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>Only return code 1 triggers the commit. Other codes fall through to the rev-list count, which
>returns False, and cmd_state_commit maps False to 'nothing to commit'.
>
> > [room.py\[749-753\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/870f10beea0d145859842b5a254b52c98d2cfb39/room.py/#L749-L753) > [room.py\[1075-1078\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/agent-room/blob/870f10beea0d145859842b5a254b52c98d2cfb39/room.py/#L1075-L1078) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >`git diff --cached --quiet` errors are mistaken for 'no changes'. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- room.py[750-751] > >## Recommended Fix >Store the result, commit when `returncode == 1`, and raise `StateError` with git's stderr when `returncode` is neither 0 nor 1. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

### The AI Code Review Platform

## Get Started
Simply sign into Github and click the "Configure" button. Check out our documentation for more info: https://docs.qodo.ai/get-started.

## Overview
Qodo automatically reviews every GitHub pull request, identifies logic bugs, edge cases, security issues, and code quality problems, and provides actionable suggestions your team can apply immediately.

Install in minutes. Integrates seamlessly into your existing workflows.

## Qodo is designed for developers who:
